query: A 43-year-old man presents requesting a sleep aid for long-standing insomnia. He says he has been having trouble falling asleep for as long as he can remember, but it has become increasingly worse after he and his wife moved to their new house. He claims that his new neighbors are jealous of his huge swimming pool and are trying to sabotage it while he sleeps. His wife even had to cancel the housewarming party that was planned for the neighbors because of her husband’s behavior. When probed further on this topic, the patient accuses the physician of being angry and hostile. What is the next best step in the management of this patient?
